sections.h2: Who sends and collects property tax bills in Lyon County, Kentucky?
sections.html:
The Lyon County Sheriff collects the bill, the Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) sets the value, and the County Clerk handles anything left unpaid after April 15. Kentucky law makes the Sheriff the collector of state, county, school and district taxes on real, tangible and intangible property (KRS 134.140 and 160.500), and the office reports about seven million dollars collected each year.

The Sheriff's Office is at 500 West Dale Avenue, Suite 100, in Eddyville, with a mailing address of PO Box 126, Eddyville, KY 42038. The PVA works from 500 B West Dale Avenue and takes calls at 270-388-7271. For delinquent bills from prior years, the Sheriff sends taxpayers to the County Clerk at 270-388-2331 for a payoff figure.

The Sheriff and the PVA both operate on West Dale Avenue in Eddyville, so a seller can often settle two questions in one trip. Call first, since the Sheriff cannot accept payment before bills arrive from the clerk at the end of September.

sections.h2: What makes Lyon County different from other Kentucky counties?
sections.html:
Lyon County is as much water as land. Of its 257 square miles, 43 are water, and the Cumberland River's Lake Barkley forms its southern edge. Eddyville is the seat, with 2,375 residents in 2020, and Kuttawa next door had 629. The two towns were rebuilt on higher ground when Barkley Dam flooded their original sites. The new Eddyville plat was filed on August 13, 1959, and every owner of land in the two flooded towns was offered a free lot in the new Eddyville.

Interstates 24 and 69 cross at Eddyville, and U.S. 62 and 641 pass through the center of town. Mineral Mound State Park sits on a peninsula in Lake Barkley, the Kentucky State Penitentiary stands on the shore south of town, and the Land Between the Lakes National Recreation Area lies across the water from Kuttawa. One school district, Lyon County Schools, covers the whole county and counted 884 students in the 2024 to 2025 year.

Weather is part of the local housing story. An EF4 tornado crossed Eddyville and Lyon County on December 10 and 11, 2021, damaging or destroying hundreds of homes and businesses, and an EF3 tornado touched down near Eddyville on May 26, 2024. Sellers of storm-damaged houses should tell the PVA about changes to the property, because the January 1 value reflects condition.

sections.h2: What do the numbers say about Lyon County homes?
sections.html:
They describe a small, older, mostly owner-held market. About four in five occupied homes are owned by the people living in them, and more than a quarter of residents are 65 or older, which is the age that unlocks the homestead exemption. The 2020 census counted 4,780 housing units and found that 30.4 percent of them were vacant.

Only five building permits were issued in the county in 2025, so new construction adds very little to the tax roll each year. Median household income of $65,066 sits above the median for Logan County, and the median home value of $189,500 is higher too. For a seller, that means a Lyon County house often has to be priced against lake access and not only square footage.

sections.h2: When are Lyon County property tax bills due?
sections.html:
Bills are due on a calendar that rewards early payment, and the Sheriff counts payments received or postmarked by each date. The Sheriff normally receives the bills from the clerk at the end of September and cannot take money earlier, so most owners see a bill in the first week of October.

  • October 1 to November 1: 2 percent discount.
  • November 2 to December 31: face amount.
  • January 1 to January 31: 5 percent penalty.
  • February 1 to April 15: 21 percent penalty.
  • After April 15: the bill must be paid at the County Clerk, where extra penalties may apply.

If no bill has arrived by October 10, the Sheriff will send a duplicate. The tax year is the calendar year, and the bill covers January 1 through December 31 of the year printed on it.

The Sheriff takes checks, money orders, cards (the card company charges a fee) and online payments. Partial payments are not accepted, although one payment can cover several bills. An unpaid balance cannot be split, so owners who struggle with the lump sum are told to check for exemptions and to ask their lender about escrow.

sections.h2: Who owes the tax when a Lyon County house changes hands?
sections.html:
The bill goes to the person who owned the property on January 1, whether or not the house has since sold. The Sheriff's guidance is that a closing agent or attorney usually computes each side's share of the year at closing. Sometimes the agent pays the Sheriff directly, and sometimes one party gets a credit and pays the bill later.

  • The Sheriff will not take a prorated payment. One or both parties must pay the full bill.
  • A mortgage company does not get the bill automatically. Lenders may pull information from the PVA tax roll, but the owner must make sure the lender receives the bill.
  • If you sold the house and a bill arrives in your name, forward it to the new owner at your old address.

Ask the closing agent in writing who will pay the Sheriff and when, and keep the receipt.

sections.h2: How do I challenge a Lyon County property assessment?
sections.html:
The owner must first confer with the PVA, then file at the County Clerk's office. State rules give the owner until the close of business on the workday after the tax roll inspection period ends, and that period starts on the first Monday in May and lasts 13 days.

After that filing, the local board of assessment appeals hears the case, usually 25 to 35 days after the inspection period. The board needs facts, such as photographs, an appraisal, insurance policies, construction costs or listings. Its written decision explains any change and tells the owner how to carry the matter to the Kentucky Board of Tax Appeals.

Ask the PVA's office at 270-388-7271 for the exact dates each spring, because the inspection window can be moved when circumstances require, and the change is advertised in the local paper.

sections.h2: Which exemptions can reduce a Lyon County tax bill?
sections.html:
The homestead and disability exemptions come first. A homeowner who is at least 65, or who is classified as totally disabled, and who lives in the home deducts $49,100 for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years. A home valued at the county's $189,500 median would then be taxed on $140,400.

The Sheriff points taxpayers with trouble paying to these exemptions and directs questions about them to the PVA at 270-388-7271. Applications go to the PVA, not to the Sheriff or the clerk. Disability applicants usually reapply each year, except veterans with a service-connected disability and people ruled totally and permanently disabled by Social Security or the Kentucky Retirement Systems.

sections.h2: How should I sell a Lyon County house that has tax due?
sections.html:
Get the payoff in writing from the right office, then let the closing agent pay it from proceeds. Current-year balances come from the Sheriff, and balances from earlier years come from the County Clerk.

Kentucky advertises delinquent bills before a sale and the county attorney mails notice, so an owner who acts early avoids added fees. Every month after April 15 adds 1 percent interest to a bill held by the clerk, and the clerk and county attorney each add a commission. Ask the closing agent to pay any recorded lien from the sale proceeds, so the house changes hands with a clean tax record.

faqs.q: Where do I pay property tax in Lyon County, Kentucky?
faqs.a: Pay the Lyon County Sheriff at 500 West Dale Avenue, Suite 100, Eddyville, or mail it to PO Box 126, Eddyville, KY 42038. You can also pay online through the link on the sheriff's tax page. After April 15 the bill must be paid at the County Clerk.

faqs.q: How much is the early payment discount in Lyon County?
faqs.a: The discount is 2 percent for payments received or postmarked from October 1 to November 1. The face amount is due from November 2 through December 31, then a 5 percent penalty starts on January 1.

faqs.q: Can I make partial payments on a Lyon County tax bill?
faqs.a: No. The Sheriff's Office cannot accept partial payments. You can pay several bills in one payment, and the Sheriff suggests checking exemptions or setting up lender escrow if the lump sum is hard to meet.

faqs.q: Who pays the property tax if I sell my Lyon County house mid-year?
faqs.a: The bill is issued in the name of the January 1 owner, and the closing agent usually prorates each party's share at the table. The Sheriff still needs the whole bill paid, so confirm in writing who will send the payment.

faqs.q: What is the Lyon County homestead exemption amount?
faqs.a: It is $49,100 for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years. It applies to owners who are 65 or older, or totally disabled, and who live in the home. Apply through the PVA at 270-388-7271.
